posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md:
Unless you have a dot matrix machine that lets you control the intrabeam angle, it would be easier to change the angle of the hologram. But that not only means changing the reference angle but the alpha, or tip angle of the master.

BTW, who do you work for? I am available for consulting, if interested PM c/o this Forum.

posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md:
Since you are working for a company doing embossed holography, I mean the former, professional consultance as you call it.

And yes, viewing angle of surface relief holograms does depend on the relative positions of the slit and reference angle during recording, and the reference angle during replay. See for example the papers by Benton and McGrew in the first Lake Forest College Symposium Proceedings.
